Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: If the source paper is not visibly stuffed inside the source cup, is there visible progress toward stuffing that paper into that cup?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image shows the matched source paper being moved toward or into the matched source cup, but not yet visibly stuffed inside it. Fail if the matched objects are assessable and there is no visible progress toward placing the paper into the cup, or the paper is already visibly stuffed inside it. Unknown if the source objects cannot be reliably matched in the edited image, or their placement or movement cannot be assessed.
node.binding: Identify the requested paper and cup by their visual and contextual roles in the source image, allowing their appearance to change in the edited image. Count only visible progress toward stuffing that paper into that cup; unrelated edits do not count.

node_traces.evidence: The source shows a white paper and a blue cup. In the edited image, the paper has been moved over and partly into the matched cup, showing progress toward stuffing it, but it is not visibly stuffed inside.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too vague and its dependency setup permits contradictory evidence to be combined: s1 says the edited objects cannot be matched, while s2 asserts a match and partial insertion. Tighten the binding to identify the source white paper and blue cup and require identity/matching to be established before either completion or progress is credited. Preserve the rubric’s distinction between complete, partial, no progress, and unresolved; do not turn an unresolved match into partial progress. Here the edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a round object, with no reliable visual match to the source paper and cup, so the evidence supports unresolved rather than a confident partial label. Check the parent/dependency routing and criteria so the aggregate decision follows the required evidence path. Treat this as visual ambiguity, not a transport or schema failure; the node executed and both supports were queried.
